page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.48xlarge is a high-performance computing server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs, utilizing AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at 3.7 GHz. The system is configured with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU scores, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, ranking in the top 10% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached read/write operations. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests.

The CPU supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-512_BF16, which contribute to top-tier prompt processing speeds in large language model inference benchmarks. However, text generation speeds for these models fall into the average to strong categories. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is supported by the 150 Gbps network interface. This profile is highly suited for high-performance computing (HPC), software compilation, molecular modeling, and parallelized simulation workloads.

It also demonstrates strong single-core capabilities and top-tier prompt processing for large language models. The hardware configuration is optimized for compute-intensive and memory-bound parallel workloads, such as software compilation, scientific simulations, and high-performance computing tasks, offering high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale parallel processing.
